content.title: What does a Mortgage Broker do? Career Overview, Roles, Jobs | AFCPE
content.text: A Mortgage Broker is a professional who acts as a intermediary between borrowers and lenders. They help borrowers obtain financing for real estate purchases by finding them suitable loan products and terms. They work with a variety of lending institutions and help match borrowers with the best lender for their specific needs and financial situation. They also assist borrowers with the loan application process, including gathering and submitting required documentation. They also negotiate loan terms and rates on behalf of their clients, often with the goal of getting the best possible terms for their clients. To become a Mortgage Broker, one typically needs to have a high school diploma or equivalent. They will also need to be licensed by the National Mortgage Licensing System (NMLS) and meet any additional state requirements. This often includes completing a pre-licensing education course and passing a background check and exam. Many states also require continuing education to maintain a valid license. Avg.
